thread:
alex (acme-corp): Hey team — our Dedicated pool for prod-app is getting lots of 429s during a traffic surge. Calls are queueing, and requests are timing out while the service is supposed to scale up. Seen since ~09:10 UTC.

mira (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you share the deployment id and any timing for the errors? Are pods stuck in Pending/ContainerCreating?

alex (acme-corp): deployment: dedicated-prod-app-42, pool: dp-west-1-a. Logs show a bunch of Pod events `ImagePullBackOff` and `Failed to pull image` followed by long backoff delays. Also saw `401 Unauthorized` a few times earlier. Token rotation happened yesterday.

mira (Support): thanks — that helps. We're triaging. Can you paste a short `kubectl describe pod` for a failing pod (no need to redact)?

alex (acme-corp): paste below:

```
Name:         prod-app-7b9f6b8c-xyz
Namespace:    default
Status:       Pending
Events:
  Type     Reason                 Age                  From               Message
  ----     ------                 ----                 ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled              3m                   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ...
  Normal   Pulling                3m                   kubelet            Pulling image \"registry.acme/corp/prod-app:latest\"
  Warning  Failed                 2m (x5 over 2m)      kubelet            Failed to pull image \"registry.acme/corp/prod-app:latest\": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to fetch token: 401 Unauthorized
  Warning  Failed                 2m (x3 over 2m)      kubelet            Error: ErrImagePull
  Warning  BackOff                1m (x10 over 1m)     kubelet            Back-off pulling image \"registry.acme/corp/prod-app:latest\"
```

sam (Eng-Runtime): interesting — from our side autoscaler saw X pending pods and began provisioning nodes, but the pods never become Ready because image pulls are failing/backing off. Autoscaler will keep adding capacity but that doesn't help if the image can't be pulled. Do you have a private registry token configured as a `imagePullSecret`?

alex (acme-corp): yes we use a private registry secret. We rotated the registry token last night as part of client-side rotation. I assumed the cluster was updated but perhaps not.

mira (Support): that explains the 401s. Two concurrent issues then: auth causing image pulls to fail (so pods never start) and scale-up looks slow because nodes are provisioning but pods still can't progress. Any sign of node provisioning errors or long `ContainerCreating` durations?

ops-bot: Autoscaler alert: pool dp-west-1-a scaled from 2 -> 8 nodes between 09:12-09:24 due to Pending pods threshold. Average node boot time: 68s.

jonathan (Eng-Infra): adding context from infra — we've seen the upstream registry enforce per-IP token rate limits recently. When a token is invalid you get repeated 401s and the client retries which can trigger throttling on the registry side. If many pods try to pull the same image at once, that can spike connection counts and hit rate limits. That combined with token failures looks like the root cause here.

sam (Eng-Runtime): noisy neighbor vector: other tenants on the same host pool were pulling large images at the same time earlier, saturating egress and contributing to slow/dropped registry connections. So even after re-applying the secret, pulls may still queue.

alex (acme-corp): ugh — ok. What's the recommended immediate mitigation? Customers are seeing 500/429s in prod.

mira (Support): immediate steps we can try: 1) rotate/update the `imagePullSecret` in the cluster to the new token (this will let new pulls authenticate), 2) increase `min_replicas` for your Dedicated service to keep warm capacity while we stabilize, 3) if you can, redeploy with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` and pin to an immutable tag (avoid `:latest`) so containers reuse local cache if present, 4) we can temporarily enable a warm pool with pre-pulled images (requires infra adjustment).

jonathan (Eng-Infra): I'll open an infra ticket to add a temporary registry mirror in dp-west-1-a to alleviate egress/rate pressure. As a short term workaround we can also pre-pull the image on existing nodes via a `DaemonSet` so subsequent pods don't need to pull at scale.

sam (Eng-Runtime): long-term action items: autoscaler heuristic update to treat long `ImagePullBackOff` as a separate signal so it triggers alerting earlier and doesn't simply keep adding nodes; and add retries/backoff tuning for registry auth failures.

alex (acme-corp): rotated secret and applied new deployment with pinned tag `prod-app@sha256:abc123` and `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`. Redeploying now.

mira (Support): thanks — any change in pod status after redeploy?

alex (acme-corp): pods are coming up, most transitioned to Running within ~45s after the redeploy. Traffic is recovering. Still watching for a few stragglers.

ops-bot: Incident note: ticket INC-4821 created for registry-mirror; assigned to Eng-Infra.

jonathan (Eng-Infra): we'll also check whether a single noisy tenant caused the bandwidth spike and, if so, throttle per-tenant pull concurrency.

sam (Eng-Runtime): for immediate perf, consider setting `min_replicas: 2` for Dedicated pools that handle blips like this — that gives faster headroom without full scale-up. Also filing a small follow-up PR to autoscaler to surface `image pull` top-level metrics to the console.

mira (Support): glad this started recovering. I'll keep the ticket open and we can close once infra mirror is live and you confirm no further 429s. Please ping if you see a recurrence. :thumbsup:

alex (acme-corp): thanks everyone — appreciate the quick responses.
